retro:
# Retrospective: PR #12717

## Effective

Bounded malicious-intent triage distinguished destructive ordinary drive reproductions from malicious instructions and avoided live execution. Fresh native Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh sessions were verified by launch and native model metadata. Both independent finals were saved before reading either. Upstream lsblk source resolved a misleading test model without real storage access. Sol's original mistaken mapping inference was corrected explicitly after source-based adjudication. Final feedback is a compact test/documentation note, not a manufactured production regression.

## Deviations retained and remediated

- Coordinator filename discovery was unnecessarily broad, exposing only filenames from historical assignments in a truncated output. No report content was read or used. Tool persistence: `/tmp/pi-bash-fe14c3edb4e2d2c0.log`. A large combined public source read also persisted at `/tmp/pi-bash-2bf463e8a65f1b6c.log`. Native history retained; use bounded assignment-local reads and the read tool rather than printing multiple large files.
- Opus exceeded the initial policy read cap with 71 total lines. Later calls respected the bound. No oversized native output notice was reported for that call.
- First fixture's awk -v replacement interpreted escapes and failed setup. Preserved and excluded; corrected run used ENVIRON literal values. Not a PR failure.
- Parent containment was incorrectly treated as individual target compliance for stock test internals. C6 stubs did not gate all own producers and used sed -i with a generated target. Summary appends and several substitutions were not gated. C5 only retained parsed values, not per-child streams. C4 semantic assertions were delayed until after the case loop despite the audit addendum saying immediately. These are actual policy deviations, not cured by seal verification or the successful runner exit.

## Assignment correction

The coordinator appended an acceptance-audit clarification to both local assignments: compare the actual fixture and each callee to the literal target/producer inventory; verify each immediate caller gates status and semantic postconditions before proceeding; retain per-child streams; use preasserted named transformation outputs, not generated sed -i paths. A report or addendum must not call guards complete merely because targets stayed under a private parent. Source-resolved findings do not require reruns solely to manufacture suite totals. No persistent reviewer memory was edited.

## Evidence acceptance

No broad stock-test, naming-table or routing totals in the public comment. Physical-partition/naming/filter/cancel assertions use source inspection. C4 raw outputs corroborate the source-derived dm limitation but do not establish native storage behavior or full process compliance. Failed evidence and both original finals remain intact. Process-only deviations do not block sound bounded feedback under current policy; completion explicitly sets safety_process_compliant=false.

## Tool issues and cleanup

No confirmed review.py or desktop tooling defect. lsblk --sysroot does not bypass explicit device-node stat, so no attempt was made to acquire real block devices. No native live disks, services, desktop slots or background fixture children used. No unrelated process cleanup, global pattern killing, browser opening or upstream action. All owned runs completed, reviewer panes preserved.
comment:
**Verified by source inspection:** the disk/physical-partition lookup, digit-suffixed partition naming and cancelled-picker exit changes address the intended paths. No new production regression was established. One new test overstates support for directly queried device-mapper mappings.

| Changed path | Before | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Disk with an encrypted descendant | Last descendant's parent can hide the disk model | Query the disk itself; physical partitions resolve to their disk |
| Partition name for `/dev/mmcblk0` | `/dev/mmcblk01` | `/dev/mmcblk0p1` |
| Empty drive-picker selection | Exit 0 | Exit 1 |

**Test/documentation correction:** In [`drive-info-test.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/1bbc248475a07bc7fe2acf0ee42735b5a5c3cea8/test/shell.d/drive-info-test.sh#L106-L110), the mapping case passes because the stub invents a parent for `lsblk -dno PKNAME /dev/root`. In [util-linux v2.42](https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/blob/v2.42/misc-utils/lsblk.c#L1829-L1854), a directly queried dm device is a root without a whole-disk parent; `-d` suppresses dependency traversal and `PKNAME` is empty.

```text
Direct dm query, source-derived behavior (not a hardware test):
new stub:  mapping -> partition -> disk model
lsblk -d: mapping -> empty PKNAME -> loop stops at mapping
```

This mapping limitation is pre-existing, not a regression in the disk/physical-partition fix. **Suggested change:** Make the stub and mapping claim reflect that scope, or implement mapping-aware traversal with an explicit policy for multiple backing devices if that capability is intended.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `1bbc2484`; production/caller inspection and upstream util-linux source. Synthetic drive-info comparisons support the disk/partition result and mapping limitation. LUKS discovery was assessed against its exact filesystem-type filter and udev-backed metadata path. No real disks, formatting, encryption changes, udev inventory or interactive password UI were exercised.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis; independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments; claims checked against source and targeted evidence, followed by a fresh Astra Medium editorial check.
